name: omb-agent
title: Multi-agent AI platform
description: A self-developing agent platform: a supervisor agent routes requests to skills and tools, answers through an OpenAI-compatible API and works from Telegram, a web chat and workflow tools.
highlights: LangGraph supervisor behind a FastAPI service; RAG microservice on LlamaIndex and a vector database
23+ reusable skills served over MCP (Model Context Protocol), with rules and a written 'constitution' for the agents
One gateway to local and cloud LLMs with tracing and evaluation of every call (Langfuse)
Skills and lessons feed back into the repository through pull requests
shows: AI-agent architecture, LLM operations, product thinking (skills as a roadmap)

name: Self-hosted Kubernetes platform
title: Platform and DevOps
description: The runtime for all my projects: 25+ services in a Kubernetes (k3d) cluster at home, described as code with a decision log and runbooks.
highlights: GitHub Actions deploys each app to the cluster; Renovate keeps images up to date
Public access only through Cloudflare Tunnel with Cloudflare Access (no open ports, e-mail allow-list)
Secrets kept out of git; metrics, dashboards and OpenTelemetry traces (VictoriaMetrics, Grafana)
Migrated from Docker Compose to Kubernetes and documented every decision
shows: DevOps and security basics, documentation discipline, migration of a live system

name: tg-bridges
title: Telegram assistant with LLM digests
description: A personal Telegram assistant: summarises unread channels into a daily digest, notifies about reactions to my posts and tracks media performance.
highlights: Digest per Telegram folder with de-duplication, token limits and editable prompts
Real-time reaction tracking and threshold alerts on media posts
Async Python (Telethon), SQLite state, any OpenAI-compatible model, graceful shutdown
Runs as a container in the cluster
shows: A complete LLM application, from requirements to production

name: Personal data pipelines
title: Small automation services
description: A set of small production services that move data between systems and run unattended.
highlights: Telegram channels to Google Photos backup that catches up on missed posts after downtime
Garmin LiveTrack e-mails (Gmail API, OAuth) to a Telegram channel, each link sent exactly once
Daily Telegram feed of new rental listings and a scheduled mirror of a closed blog with a git archive
Scheduled jobs, idempotent processing and alerts before token expiry
shows: API integration, reliability and idempotency, scheduled ETL
